title: GS21 hump in a leverage index (b~ - 0.5 z~)^2, gs_bv -0.2, cap 4, gs_qcomp 0
question: Does a square in the leverage index that the observed lev characteristic tracks give the leverage hump room and a gap?
notes:
WHY (2026-11-05). The leverage humps in the coupon alone (gvylqm/lqh/lqc) leave absolute room of 0.02-0.12 in Sharpe against 0.25-0.31 for the GS21 economies that work, because a coupon fixed for life and uniform on [0.1, 0.9] gives b~^2 a range of only [0, 1.9] and no time variation. The analog of what worked (gvyzzh10, the square of productivity: tails to 9, time-varying, revealed by ROE and size; KP's lesson that the dispersion of the characteristic the exposure multiplies is the strongest lever) is a square in a LEVERAGE INDEX L = b~ - k z~: high coupon and low productivity are both high leverage, and the observed lev = b / P moves with exactly that combination because P falls with z. The exposure gs_bv (L^2 - 1 - k^2) is written with the existing terms: gs_bzq 1 (b~^2 - 1), gs_bzb -2k (z~ b~), gs_bzz k^2 (z~^2 - 1). gs_bv < 0 is a hump in market leverage, the sign that worked for productivity (gvyzzh10). This economy: k 0.5, gs_bv -0.2, cap 4, compensation 0.

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; ids filled from the Quest build log by the solve script before any seed runs.

PREDICTION (2026-11-05): the premium across lev quintiles is hump-shaped; room 30% or more and a fair gap at or above +0.029. FALSIFIED if room is at or below 10% on three seeds.
